Hedging cost £825,967 vs going naked (85% mandate price). 7225 bill shock events (1740 in crisis years); 78/110 retention offers accepted.

insights.headline: Hedging cost £825,967 vs going naked (85% mandate price)
insights.narrative: Whole-run commodity basis: actual net £446,579 vs naked £1,272,546. The 85% minimum hedge mandate cost £825,967 over the 10-year window. Worst year: 2023 (hedging cost £159,597 vs naked). Hedging reduces variance (survival objective) at the cost of expected P&L.

insights.headline: 7225 bill shock events (1740 in crisis years); 78/110 retention offers accepted
insights.narrative: Bill shocks across 2016-2025: 7225 events, 1555 extreme (>100%). 2021-22 accounted for 1740 shocks as wholesale prices spiked. Retention: 78/110 offers accepted (71%); 68 customers churned without an offer (margin guard blocked). Enterprise value: £416,666 across 231 accounts.

insights.headline: Risk committee: 0 interventions; SURVIVED full 2016-2025 window
insights.narrative: The risk committee (Context Handshake) intervened 0 times over 10 years, with 0 in the 2021-22 crisis. Business survived: No administration event -- Ofgem solvency floor maintained.. The 85% minimum hedge mandate limited worst-case exposure.

insights.headline: Net margin £543,474 (23.4% of total revenue -- above 2-5% benchmark)
insights.narrative: Gross margin £1,388,221, net £543,474 (23.4% of revenue). Industry benchmark: 2-5% -- this business sits above that range. I&C customers contribute 0% of net margin (£0); residential 100% (£543,474). Cost to serve: £175,046; net after CTS: £368,428.

insights.headline: 39084 bills issued; service quality 0.923/1.0, clarity 0.874/1.0
insights.narrative: 39084 bills issued over 2016-2025 (avg 3908/yr). Service quality: 0.923 (excellent). Bill clarity: 0.874 (good). Cost to serve: £175,046 portfolio total, £758/account/run.

coherence_narrative: The dominant theme is crisis survival. The business survived the full 2016-2025 window including the 2021-22 energy crisis, with the 85% hedge mandate cost £825,967 vs going naked, 1740 bill shocks in the 2021-22 crisis, and 78/110 retention offers accepted. net margin £543,474 (23.4% of revenue -- above 2-5% benchmark), with I&C customers contributing 0% of net margin. The hedging mandate limited worst-case downside at the cost of expected P&L in calmer years; the I&C book was the primary profit engine throughout. The book is well-diversified between residential and I&C segments.
recommended_actions: I&C margin share 0%: diversified book -- maintain residential acquisition to keep I&C below 70% dependency
Hedge cost £825,967 over 10 years -- mandate is a survival insurance premium, not an expected-value strategy
1740 crisis-year bill shocks: consider tariff smoothing mechanism to spread 2021-22 wholesale spike across 2020-2023 for residential customers
